decision.explanation: Polynomial division gives (x²+5x+1)/(x+3)=x+2−5/(x+3). Integrating term by term gives x²/2+2x−5ln|x+3|+C, matching option e.

after.name: Question 1
after.worked_solution:
We first need to decompose the integrand into its quotient and remainder parts, which we can do using synthetic division.

We draw up a synthetic division table:

$$
\begin{aligned} & {x}^{2} & {x}^{1} & {x}^{0} \\ -3 & 1 & 5 & 1 \\  & ↓ & -3 & -6 \\  & 1 & 2 & -5\end{aligned}
$$

So from the synthetic division, we get that

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}+5x+1}{x+3}=x+2-\frac{5}{x+3}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{x}^{2}+5x+1}{x+3}\,\text{d}x & =\int (x+2-\frac{5}{x+3})\text{d}x \\  & =\int x\,\text{d}x+2\int \text{d}x-5\int \frac{1}{x+3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}+2x-5\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+3|+C.\end{aligned}
$$

content.worked_solution:
We first need to decompose the integrand into its quotient and remainder parts, which we can do using synthetic division.

We draw up a synthetic division table:

$$
\begin{aligned} & {x}^{2} & {x}^{1} & {x}^{0} \\ -3 & 1 & 5 & 1 \\  & ↓ & -3 & -6 \\  & 1 & 2 & -5\end{aligned}
$$

So from the synthetic division, we get that

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}+5x+1}{x+3}=x+2-\frac{5}{x+3}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{x}^{2}+5x+1}{x+3}\,\text{d}x & =\int (x+2-\frac{5}{x+3})\text{d}x \\  & =\int x\,\text{d}x+2\int \text{d}x-5\int \frac{1}{x+3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}+2x-5\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+3|+C.\end{aligned}
$$

after.worked_solution:
First, we pull out the factor of $2$ from the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{x+2}{2x-3}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{x+2}{2(x-\frac{3}{2})}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\int \frac{x+2}{(x-\frac{3}{2})}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we draw up our synthetic division table to decompose the integrand into its quotient and remainder.

$$
\begin{aligned} & x & {x}^{0} \\ \frac{3}{2} & 1 & 2 \\  & ↓ & \frac{3}{2} \\  & 1 & \frac{7}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

So from the synthetic division, we get that

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x+2}{(x-\frac{3}{2})} & =1+\frac{(\frac{7}{2})}{(x-\frac{3}{2})} \\  & =1+\frac{7}{2(x-\frac{3}{2})} \\  & =1+\frac{7}{2x-3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{x+2}{2x-3}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{2}\int (1+\frac{7}{2x-3})\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\int \text{d}x+7\int \frac{1}{2x-3}\,\text{d}x] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[x+\frac{7}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|2x-3|]+C \\  & =\frac{x}{2}+\frac{7}{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡|2x-3|+C.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned} & x & {x}^{0} \\ -\frac{2}{3} & 1 & 1 \\  & ↓ & -\frac{2}{3} \\  & 1 & \frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x+1}{(x+\frac{2}{3})} & =1+\frac{(\frac{1}{3})}{(x+\frac{2}{3})} \\  & =1+\frac{1}{3(x+\frac{2}{3})} \\  & =1+\frac{1}{3x+2}.\end{aligned}

$$

content.worked_solution:
First, we pull out the factor of $3$ from the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{x+1}{3x+2}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{x+1}{3(x+\frac{2}{3})}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\int \frac{x+1}{(x+\frac{2}{3})}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we draw up our synthetic division table to decompose the integrand into its quotient and remainder.

$$
\begin{aligned} & x & {x}^{0} \\ -\frac{2}{3} & 1 & 1 \\  & ↓ & -\frac{2}{3} \\  & 1 & \frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

So from the synthetic division, we get that

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x+1}{(x+\frac{2}{3})} & =1+\frac{(\frac{1}{3})}{(x+\frac{2}{3})} \\  & =1+\frac{1}{3(x+\frac{2}{3})} \\  & =1+\frac{1}{3x+2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{x+1}{3x+2}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{3}\int (1+\frac{1}{3x+2})\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[\int \text{d}x+\int \frac{1}{3x+2}\,\text{d}x] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[x+\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡|3x+2|]+C \\  & =\frac{x}{3}+\frac{1}{9}\operatorname{ln}⁡|3x+2|+C.\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: The integrand equals 1/7−1/[7(7x+1)]. Integrating gives x/7−(1/49)ln|7x+1|+C, matching option e.

after.name: Question 4
after.worked_solution:
First, we pull out the factor of $7$ from the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{x}{7x+1}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{x}{7(x+\frac{1}{7})}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{7}\int \frac{x}{(x+\frac{1}{7})}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we draw up our synthetic division table to decompose the integrand into its quotient and remainder.

$$
\begin{aligned} & x & {x}^{0} \\ -\frac{1}{7} & 1 & 0 \\  & ↓ & -\frac{1}{7} \\  & 1 & -\frac{1}{7}\end{aligned}
$$

So from the synthetic division, we get that

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{(x+\frac{1}{7})} & =1+\frac{(-\frac{1}{7})}{(x+\frac{1}{7})} \\  & =1-\frac{1}{7(x+\frac{1}{7})} \\  & =1-\frac{1}{7x+1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{x}{7x+1}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{7}\int (1-\frac{1}{7x+1})\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{7}[\int \text{d}x-\int \frac{1}{7x+1}\,\text{d}x] \\  & =\frac{1}{7}[x-\frac{1}{7}\operatorname{ln}⁡|7x+1|]+C \\  & =\frac{x}{7}-\frac{1}{49}\operatorname{ln}⁡|7x+1|+C.\end{aligned}
$$

content.worked_solution:
First, we pull out the factor of $7$ from the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{x}{7x+1}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{x}{7(x+\frac{1}{7})}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{7}\int \frac{x}{(x+\frac{1}{7})}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we draw up our synthetic division table to decompose the integrand into its quotient and remainder.

$$
\begin{aligned} & x & {x}^{0} \\ -\frac{1}{7} & 1 & 0 \\  & ↓ & -\frac{1}{7} \\  & 1 & -\frac{1}{7}\end{aligned}
$$

So from the synthetic division, we get that

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{(x+\frac{1}{7})} & =1+\frac{(-\frac{1}{7})}{(x+\frac{1}{7})} \\  & =1-\frac{1}{7(x+\frac{1}{7})} \\  & =1-\frac{1}{7x+1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{x}{7x+1}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{7}\int (1-\frac{1}{7x+1})\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{7}[\int \text{d}x-\int \frac{1}{7x+1}\,\text{d}x] \\  & =\frac{1}{7}[x-\frac{1}{7}\operatorname{ln}⁡|7x+1|]+C \\  & =\frac{x}{7}-\frac{1}{49}\operatorname{ln}⁡|7x+1|+C.\end{aligned}
$$
